items.pronunciation_notes: Two vowels running together with no consonant between them: jaa-o.

learn.explanation_en: Hindi has no single word for go. It has three, and which one you use says everything about your relationship with the person you are speaking to: जा for तू, जाओ for तुम, and जाइए for आप. There is no neutral option and no way to avoid choosing, which is why the register system from Module 5 turns out to matter more here than anywhere else in the course. जाओ is the तुम form, built by adding -ओ to the stem, and it is the one you will use with friends, with people your own age, and with anyone who has already used it on you.

examples.note: The तुम form — stem plus -ओ.
The destination takes no postposition, as always with जाना.
Same shape, and no word for to is needed.

common_error.why_en: An imperative takes no auxiliary and usually no pronoun either. The form alone is the whole sentence.

practice.prompt_en: Give the imperative for this register.
practice.question: जाना · तुम · imperative
practice.explanation_en: The तुम imperative is the stem plus -ओ. जाओगे is the future, not a command.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the simple future cell?
game.explanation_en: तुम जाओगे — you will go. जाओ is a command about now.

items.pronunciation_notes: The stem vowel stays long and the ending is short: bo-lo.
items.gloss_en: the तुम imperative on a consonant stem

learn.explanation_en: बोलना gives बोलो, सुनना gives सुनो, बैठना gives बैठो. There is nothing to agree with here — no gender, no number, no auxiliary — because a command is aimed at whoever is in front of you and Hindi does not mark anything further. That makes the imperative the only part of the verb system in this module with no agreement at all, which after twenty-five levels of participles and auxiliaries is a genuine rest.

examples.note: Also used to mean go ahead, I am listening.
Very often used simply to get someone's attention.
The casual version of an offer you will hear constantly.

common_error.why_en: बोलते is the habitual participle and needs an auxiliary behind it. The imperative is built from the bare stem instead.

practice.prompt_en: Give the imperative for this register.
practice.question: सुनना · तुम · imperative
practice.explanation_en: Stem सुन plus -ओ. सुन alone is the तू form and सुनिए is the आप form.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: तुम बोलते हो — you speak, as a habit.

items.pronunciation_notes: यहाँ ends on a nasal hum and runs straight into the vowel of आओ.
items.gloss_en: the imperative with a place word

learn.explanation_en: यहाँ आओ is come here, and it shows the ordinary shape of an imperative sentence: everything else first, verb last. That is the same word order you have used since Module 5 and nothing about a command changes it. Worth knowing about tone, too. A bare imperative in Hindi is not as blunt as its English translation looks — यहाँ आओ between friends carries no more force than come here does, and adding ज़रा or a rising tone softens it further, exactly as it would in English.

examples.note: Place word first, verb last.
The same shape with a different verb.
आना takes its destination bare, exactly as जाना does.

common_error.why_en: The verb goes last. Reversing it is understandable but sounds like an afterthought rather than a request.

practice.prompt_en: Give the imperative for this register.
practice.question: आना · तुम · imperative

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: तुम यहाँ आ रहे हो — you are coming here right now.

summary.recap_en: The imperative has three forms chosen entirely by register, and the तुम one is the stem plus -ओ. It is the only part of the verb system with no agreement at all — no gender, no number, no auxiliary — and the verb still goes last in the sentence.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the आप form, which is the one to default to and the one with the irregulars.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three vowels in a row with no consonant at all: aa-i-e, and the last is short.
items.gloss_en: the polite imperative, and the safe default

learn.title_en: The most useful polite word in Hindi
learn.explanation_en: आइए is please come, or please come in, and it is the word that greets you at every doorway in India. The आप imperative is the stem plus -इए, and it is the form to default to with anyone you do not already know — the same rule Module 5 gave you for the pronoun itself. It is worth over-learning this ending, because an imperative in the wrong register is far more noticeable than a wrong tense. Getting the grammar slightly off sounds foreign; getting the register wrong sounds rude.

examples.note: Stem आ plus -इए.
The polite version of the sentence from the last level.
This is how you get a stranger's attention politely.

common_error.why_en: आओ is the तुम form. Opening with आप and finishing with a casual imperative is the mismatch most likely to land badly.

practice.prompt_en: Give the imperative for this register.
practice.question: आना · आप · imperative
practice.explanation_en: The आप imperative is the stem plus -इए. आएंगे is the future rather than a request.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the simple future cell?
game.explanation_en: आप आएंगे — you will come. आइए is a request about now.

items.pronunciation_notes: The stem vowel lengthens to a long ii, which is the whole irregularity: kii-ji-e.

learn.title_en: Four verbs break the rule, and only four
learn.explanation_en: By the rule, करना should give करिए. It gives कीजिए instead. The same thing happens to three more: लेना becomes लीजिए, देना becomes दीजिए, and पीना becomes पीजिए. That is the complete list — every other verb in the language is regular here, so this is four words to memorise rather than a pattern to worry about. All four are high-frequency, which is exactly why they are irregular: the words people say most often are the ones that wear down.

examples.note: करना, and the ending swallows the stem's vowel.

examples.english: please take it, here you are
examples.note: What someone says as they hand you something.
The polite way to ask for anything at a counter.

common_error.why_en: करिए is what the rule predicts and it is not what people say. This is one of exactly four verbs where that happens.

practice.prompt_en: Give the imperative for this register.
practice.question: करना · आप · imperative
practice.explanation_en: करना is one of the four irregulars, so कीजिए rather than the predicted करिए.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: आप करते हैं — you do it, as a habit.

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex and aspirated in the middle, then two short vowels: bai-ṭhi-e.
items.gloss_en: the polite imperative on a consonant stem

learn.explanation_en: बैठिए is what you will be told within seconds of entering anyone's home or office, and it is worth recognising instantly. The stem बैठ ends in a consonant so the ending simply attaches: बैठ plus इए. Compare it with बैठा है from level fourteen, which describes someone already seated, and you have the two things you can do with this verb — invite the action, or describe its result. The middle case, बैठ रहा है, is the one you will almost never need.

examples.note: Stem बैठ plus -इए, with nothing merged.
Place word first, verb last, as always.
Said to invite someone to speak — the polite version of बोलो.

common_error.why_en: बैठो is the तुम form. Offering someone a seat in the wrong register undercuts the courtesy of offering at all.

practice.prompt_en: Give the imperative for this register.
practice.question: बैठना · आप · imperative
practice.explanation_en: Consonant stem, so the ending attaches with no change: बैठिए.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह बैठा है — he is seated, the result of a completed action.

summary.recap_en: The आप imperative is the stem plus -इए and it is the form to default to with anyone you do not know. Four verbs break the rule — कीजिए, लीजिए, दीजिए, पीजिए — and that list is closed. A wrong register here is more noticeable to a listener than a wrong tense.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the तू form, which comes with a warning, and how to tell someone not to.

items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable and nothing else — the bare stem, with no ending at all.
items.gloss_en: the तू imperative, taught as a warning

learn.title_en: The bare stem, and when not to use it
learn.explanation_en: The तू imperative is the stem with nothing added: जा, कर, बोल, सुन. It is the shortest form in the language and the one to be most careful with. Module 5 taught तू as a warning rather than an option, and that applies double here — a bare imperative to someone who expects तुम or आप reads as contempt, not informality. You will hear it constantly, between close friends, from parents to small children, and in film dialogue, so you need to recognise it. Producing it is a different matter, and the honest advice is not to, until a Hindi speaker uses it on you first.

examples.note: The bare stem. Recognise it; think twice before saying it.
Between close friends this is affectionate rather than harsh.
The same sentence you learnt with आओ, two registers down.

common_error.why_en: Not a grammatical error — a social one. With anyone you have just met, the bare stem is the wrong choice however correct it looks.

practice.prompt_en: Give the imperative for this register.
practice.question: बोलना · तू · imperative
practice.explanation_en: The तू imperative is the bare stem, with no ending added.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the simple future cell?
game.explanation_en: वह जाएगा — he will go. The other three are commands in three different registers.

items.pronunciation_notes: मत is short and flat, and the stress falls on the verb behind it: mat jaa-o.
items.gloss_en: negative imperatives use मत, not नहीं

learn.explanation_en: Everywhere else in this module, नहीं has been the negative. Commands are the exception: they take मत instead. मत जाओ is do not go, and नहीं जाओ is simply not something people say. Module 5 gave you नहीं, न and मत as three separate words, and this is what मत was for — it exists only to negate an instruction. The placement is the same as always, directly in front of the verb, so the only thing to change is which word you reach for.

examples.note: मत in front, and the imperative unchanged behind it.
मत sits directly in front of the verb, not at the start of the sentence.
The same shape with another verb.

common_error.why_en: नहीं negates statements. An instruction takes मत, and using the wrong one is immediately audible.

practice.question: जाओ · negative
practice.explanation_en: मत goes directly in front of the verb, exactly where नहीं goes in a statement.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the simple future cell?
game.explanation_en: तुम नहीं जाओगे — you will not go, which is a statement and so takes नहीं.

items.pronunciation_notes: The short मत followed by three vowels: mat jaa-i-e.

learn.explanation_en: मत जा, मत जाओ, मत जाइए — one negative word across all three registers, with the imperative behind it doing the register work as usual. So there is nothing extra to learn for the polite negative, which is worth knowing because telling someone politely not to do something is a fairly common thing to need. The whole imperative system now fits in one line: three forms by register, one negative word in front, verb last, and no agreement anywhere.

examples.note: मत plus the आप imperative.
The polite version of the sentence from the last item.
The तू version — same negative, lowest register.

common_error.why_en: जाएंगे is the future, which is a prediction rather than an instruction. मत only ever attaches to an imperative.

practice.question: मत जाओ · आप
practice.explanation_en: The negative word is unchanged; only the imperative moves up a register.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: आप नहीं जाते — you do not go, with the auxiliary dropped after नहीं as usual.

summary.recap_en: The imperative system is three forms chosen by register — bare stem, stem plus -ओ, stem plus -इए — with मत in front for the negative and no agreement anywhere. मत is for instructions and नहीं is for statements, and that is the only place in the course where the two part company.
summary.next_up_en: Next: होना's own perfective, which is irregular and turns up in the question you will ask most often.

items.pronunciation_notes: हुआ is two short vowels with no consonant between: hu-aa.

learn.explanation_en: होना means to be, but its perfective हुआ means happened or became — the completed version of being something is having become it. क्या हुआ is what happened, and it is one of the handful of sentences you will use every single day. The form is irregular: the rule would predict होया, and the actual participle is हुआ, with the stem vowel changed. होना is the second of the two irregular intransitive perfectives, alongside गया from level fourteen, and between them that is the whole list.

examples.note: The bare perfective, and by far the commonest use of this word.
The standard reply, with नहीं in its usual place in front of the verb.
With है the result is still standing — something is currently wrong.

common_error.why_en: होया is what the rule predicts and it is not a word. होना and जाना are the two verbs where the perfective is built from a changed stem.

practice.question: होना · masculine singular · perfective
practice.explanation_en: हुआ, with the stem vowel changed. होता is the habitual participle.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective present cell?
game.explanation_en: क्या हुआ है — the perfective participle with a present auxiliary.

items.pronunciation_notes: कैसे opens with a diphthong close to the vowel in English 'kite': kai-se.

learn.title_en: हुआ agrees like any other perfective
learn.explanation_en: There is nothing special about हुआ beyond its shape. It takes the same four endings as every other perfective participle — हुआ, हुई, हुए, हुईं — and agrees with whatever the subject is. यह कैसे हुआ asks how this happened, with हुआ agreeing with the masculine यह. Change the subject and the participle follows: बात कैसे हुई, because बात is feminine. The irregularity is entirely in the stem and not at all in the agreement.

examples.note: यह is masculine here, so हुआ.
बात is feminine, so the participle turns to हुई.
A different question word in the same slot.

common_error.why_en: बात is one of the feminine nouns Module 4 asked you to memorise, and the perfective agrees with it like any other participle.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: होना · बात · perfective
practice.explanation_en: बात is feminine and singular, so the participle is हुई.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: यह कैसे होता है — how does this happen, as a general fact.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three light syllables and then the heavy थ: kyaa hu-aa thaa.
items.gloss_en: होना has a full perfective row of its own

learn.explanation_en: क्या हुआ था is what had happened, and it looks odd at first because होना is appearing twice — once as the participle हुआ and once as the auxiliary था. That is perfectly normal. होना is a verb like any other and has its own full row: हुआ, हुआ है, हुआ था, हुआ होगा. The auxiliary in each case is a second, separate होना doing its ordinary job. Once you see that, nothing in the module is left unexplained — every cell of the grid, for every verb including this one, is built the same way.

examples.note: The participle and the auxiliary are both from होना.
The bare form, which is what you want with a named past time.
The presumptive, completing होना's own row.

common_error.why_en: The participle comes first and the auxiliary sits behind it, exactly as with every other verb in the module.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: होना · यह · masculine · perfective past
practice.explanation_en: Perfective participle हुआ with the past auxiliary था.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective presumptive cell?
game.explanation_en: यह हुआ होगा — this has probably happened.

summary.recap_en: होना's perfective is हुआ, irregular in its stem and entirely regular in its agreement. It means happened or became, it carries a full row of its own — हुआ, हुआ है, हुआ था, हुआ होगा — and with गया it makes up the complete list of irregular intransitive perfectives.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the regular rule restated, and the four irregular participles you will need to recognise before you can use them.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both syllables are light and the stress is even: cha-laa.

learn.title_en: Almost every verb is regular here
learn.explanation_en: चलना gives चला, उठना gives उठा, बैठना gives बैठा, सोना gives सोया. The rule from level fourteen has held throughout: stem plus -आ, with a य inserted if the stem ends in a vowel. It is worth stating plainly how few exceptions there are. In the whole language, six verbs form their perfective irregularly — जाना, होना, करना, देना, लेना and पीना — and you have already met the two that are intransitive. Everything else in Hindi follows the rule without exception.

examples.note: Consonant stem, so -आ attaches directly.
The same shape with another consonant stem.
Vowel stem, so a य appears between.

common_error.why_en: चलाया is a different verb — चलाना, meaning to drive or operate something. Adding a syllable changes the word rather than the tense.

practice.question: उठना · masculine singular · perfective
practice.explanation_en: Consonant stem उठ plus -आ. उठाया belongs to a different verb meaning to lift.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual past cell?
game.explanation_en: वह चलता था — he used to walk.

items.pronunciation_notes: The stem vowel shortens and a य bridges: ki-yaa, two light syllables.
items.gloss_en: four irregular participles to recognise, not yet to use

learn.title_en: You can learn these, but you cannot use them yet
learn.explanation_en: The remaining four irregular perfectives are किया from करना, दिया from देना, लिया from लेना, and पिया from पीना. Learn the forms now, because you will meet them in everything you read. But do not build sentences with them yet, and here is the honest reason: all four are transitive, and a transitive verb in the perfective takes the ने construction, which changes the subject and stops the verb agreeing with it. मैं किया is wrong; the sentence you want is मैंने किया, and that ने has a whole module to itself. So this is a vocabulary item rather than a grammar one — recognise these four, and wait.

examples.note: From करना. The predicted form करा exists but means something else.
From लेना, with the same shortening and य.
From देना, and the pattern is identical.

common_error.why_en: A transitive verb in the perfective needs ने on the subject. That construction arrives in Module 9, which is why these four are recognition only for now.

practice.question: लेना · masculine singular · perfective
practice.explanation_en: लिया, with the stem vowel shortened. लेया is what the rule predicts and is not a word.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह करता है — he does it. The participle किया cannot yet stand in a sentence of its own.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two vowels sliding into each other with no consonant: hu-aa.
items.gloss_en: an imperative, a question and a guess in four lines

learn.title_en: Four lines, four different things the module taught
learn.explanation_en: This short exchange uses an imperative, an irregular perfective, a negated perfective and a presumptive, which between them cover most of the last fifteen levels. Watch the last line in particular: होगी is a guess, not a statement, and the speaker is telling you they do not actually know where the sister is. English would need a whole extra word for that — probably, must be — and Hindi puts it in the verb, so the choice is unavoidable and the information is always there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: Your sister has not come home.

common_error.why_en: है would claim to know. The speaker is guessing, and Hindi marks that difference in the verb rather than with an extra word.

practice.question: बहन घर नहीं ___।
practice.explanation_en: बहन is feminine and singular, so the perfective participle is आई.

game.question_en: Listen to the second line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: The speaker says हुआ — the irregular perfective of होना, in its bare form.

summary.recap_en: Six verbs in the whole language form their perfective irregularly: जाना, होना, करना, देना, लेना and पीना. The two intransitive ones are fully usable now; the four transitive ones are recognition only until Module 9 supplies the ने construction they need.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last two levels of the module, drilling the irregular forms and pulling the whole grid together.
